With @Peter Pfaffelhuber , we are launching a probability theory formalization project and we would like to invite anyone interested to collaborate.
The goal is to formalize the definition of a Brownian motion, a stochastic process on the positive real line which is an important object in probability theory.

Some links:

  • github repository of the project
  • blueprint with a detailed description of the construction
  • zulip channel for discussion

The project contains two mostly independent parts, that we then bring together to finish the construction:

  • a first part with results about Gaussian distributions. Mathlib does not have multivariate Gaussians yet, and we need those.
  • a Kolmogorov-Chentsov continuity theorem. The blueprint mostly follows a recent paper [Krätschmer, Urusov, 2023] that contains a general form of the continuity theorem for metric spaces, instead of a more usual version specialized to R^d. The proof uses Talagrand's chaining techniques.

See the blueprint for more details, and please come to the zulip channel to discuss the formalization!

The formalization of a Brownian motion on the non-negative real half line has been completed this summer! :tada:
But we are not stopping there, and we are actively working on setting up the theory of stochastic calculus. The main goal is Itô's lemma. If you are interested in continuous time martingales and stopping times and in formalizing the definition of stochastic integrals, you should come and contribute!

We have open issues that you could work on, and the issues with the label good-first-issue should be easy entry points (read the contributing guide to learn how to claim an issue). You can also have a look at the blueprint.
Come over to the project zulip channel to discuss the formalization.

If you are curious about the completed work about Brownian motion, you can look at the blueprint or the code for the fully detailed description of the theorems and proofs. We also have a short description of the results (still in construction, very succinct for now). A preprint about the project is coming soon.
